summary: Add the plugin store contract and the GitHub plugin's mirror and read API: the member that polls a repository keeps every pull request's and issue's facts, head history and keyed events in <state>/plugins/github/github.sqlite3 and serves /v1/plugins/github/* and st gh prs, pr and checks from it; other members relay those reads to it. Readers take a newer vcs.item.state (and the github.event merge-queue-left key) over resource.observed. The mirror refills from GitHub itself when it is new, moved, restored or behind. Nothing stops being written.

replay.detail: No claim is rewritten or replayed. Two kinds are registered, vcs.item.state and github.event, and no build writes them yet; resource.observed snapshots are written exactly as before.

schema.detail: Claim registry: new kinds vcs.item.state (resource subjects, system-only, append, fixed compact field set) and github.event (new subject family github-event, system-only, once), and retention entries for both with no checkpoint rule, so the checkpoint rules digest is unchanged. Claims database: the resource projection's pending triggers move to version 2 (they also mark subjects of vcs.item.state); a store reopened with older triggers queues every subject with a vcs.item.state claim once. No storage version change. Plugin file: github.sqlite3 gains plugin_meta (mirror_version 1) and the mirror_repositories, mirror_items, mirror_heads, mirror_events and mirror_event_keys tables; its PRAGMA user_version stays 1. A file with a newer mirror version is set aside and replaced, as a newer cursor version already was.

rules.detail: No checkpoint rule or rules digest changes: the new kinds are listed under [kinds] only, pending until the poller writes them. No fleet barrier or coordinated upgrade.

compatibility.detail: Contract changes C6 (read side) and C9 from the db break-up plan. New, additive: routes GET /v1/plugins/github/repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls, /pulls/{number}, /pulls/{number}/checks and /events; CLI st gh prs, pr and checks; daemon.started features.github_plugin=1 and /v1/health features.github_plugin=1; peer client read capability github-plugin version 1 with the GithubPlugin relay operation. Readers of an item's facts (the resource projection behind /v1/client/resources, the actual-state fold unpinned resource gates read, attention on a pull request, the idle hold's merge-queue check) take a vcs.item.state accepted no earlier than the item's newest resource.observed over the observed facts; until a poller writes it (step 3b) they read exactly what they read before. Mixed versions need no barrier: a member of this build relays only to a poller that advertises github_plugin and whose relay hop grants github-plugin; beside an older poller, an unreachable poller or a read with no person or agent, it answers from its own graph with source.kind=graph and the reason. An older member never receives the new relay operation and never sees the new kinds written. Tested beside the previous published release (fleet::previous_release_poller_beside_a_github_plugin_member_and_its_upgrade).

downtime.detail: No startup migration of the claims store beyond reinstalling four triggers; the plugin file's mirror tables are created on first start. After its first look, each polled repository's mirror refills from GitHub with one fresh look recorded nowhere else (on a repository of about 730 open items: about 8 REST and 8 GraphQL pages, under the observer's request budget). Until then its reads answer from the graph and say so.

manual.detail: No operator action on upgrade. The mirror lives only on the member that polls a repository. The plugin store is not in the graph's backup, and needs no restore: a restored, moved or new poller refills its mirror from GitHub, the graph keeps every delivery and the facts other members read, and each observer's claim keeps its read position. A lost mirror loses only head history of pull requests closed before the refill, events older than it, and full facts of closed items it never sees again. A set-aside github.sqlite3.set-aside-* file may be deleted.

recovery.detail: Rolling back to the previous release is supported. The previous release opens github.sqlite3 (user_version 1), reads its cursors and ignores the mirror tables; it reinstalls its own resource triggers, and claims of the new kinds a later build writes it keeps as unknown records and does not read. Upgrading again finds each mirror behind the poll cursor the older build moved, answers from the graph until it has refilled from GitHub, and requeues the subjects of any vcs.item.state claims. The mirror may be deleted at any time: the poller refills it from GitHub.
